units.title: Numeric transforms and categorical encoding
outcomes: Build a leakage-safe numeric and categorical preprocessing path with fitted state, unknown-category behavior and schema tests.
Choose scaling, clipping and imputation for skewed, heavy-tailed and missing features and state what each choice hides.
Keep sparse categorical output sparse through the pipeline and densify only where the estimator requires it.
units.why: Every estimator downstream sees the transformed geometry, not the raw table. A scaler fit on the wrong rows or an encoder that errors on new categories breaks serving before any model runs.

study.title: Missing-value strategies and indicators
study.locator: 8.4.2 univariate median and most_frequent strategies; 8.4.6 AddIndicator for keeping a missingness flag beside the imputed value; 8.4.7 which estimators accept NaN directly

focus: Fit every statistic on training rows only, then transform the rest. Refitting on evaluation rows leaks their distribution into the features.
OneHotEncoder with handle_unknown=ignore writes a new category as all zeros; with handle_unknown=error it raises. Pick one before serving.
StandardScaler centers, so it densifies sparse input unless with_mean=False. MaxAbsScaler preserves sparsity.
A missingness indicator keeps the fact of missingness after imputation fills the value. Dropping the flag assumes missingness carries no signal.
units.reproduce: Closed-book, build a two-column pipeline on five training rows: median-impute and standardize a numeric column, one-hot encode a categorical column with handle_unknown=ignore. Transform two new rows, one with an unseen category and one with a missing number, and write the exact output rows including the all-zeros encoding.
traps: Fitting the imputer or scaler on the full data before splitting. Validation scores then reuse evaluation statistics.
Setting sparse_output=False on a high-cardinality encoder inside a pipeline. Memory grows with rows times categories; keep sparse until an estimator needs dense.
Reading the percentile-flattened income as deleting outliers. It remaps tails to fixed bins; the IsolationForest drop in the same notebook is a separate commented-out choice.

selfTest.q: A scaler fit on all 10,000 rows gives mean 5.2; fit on the 8,000 training rows gives 5.0. Which one goes into the pipeline, and why?
selfTest.a: The training-only 5.0. The full-data mean carries evaluation rows into every transformed training value.

selfTest.q: OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown=ignore) trained on [a, b] sees [c]. What row does it emit, and what does inverse_transform return for it?
selfTest.a: It emits [0, 0]. inverse_transform maps all zeros back to None when no category was dropped. Verified with scikit-learn 1.9.

selfTest.q: Why does StandardScaler on a CSR matrix raise unless with_mean=False?
selfTest.a: Centering subtracts the mean from every entry including stored zeros, which would densify the matrix. With with_mean=False only scaling applies and sparsity survives.

selfTest.q: When does an imputed column need a companion indicator column?
selfTest.a: When missingness itself predicts the target, for example sensors that fail under load. The indicator keeps that signal after the value is filled.

study.title: Selection and persistence
study.locator: Exercise 3 SelectFromModel with threshold=0.005 in the preparation pipeline; Model persistence using joblib with the production-script pattern
study.depth: Treat the 0.005 threshold as a starting point, not an optimum: the notebook reports no gain there. Skip Exercises 1, 2 and 4 here.

focus: Selection inside the pipeline is fit on training folds only. Selecting on all rows before cross-validation picks features with evaluation help.
ColumnTransformer drops unlisted columns by default under remainder=drop. Name every kept column or set remainder explicitly.
ClusterSimilarity and ratio features are fit state too: their centers and medians come from training rows and must serialize with the pipeline.
joblib saves the fitted object, not the build script. Reload in a fresh process and compare predictions before trusting the artifact.
units.reproduce: Closed-book, sketch a ColumnTransformer with a median-plus-scaler numeric path and a most-frequent-plus-one-hot categorical path, state the remainder behavior, and write the three-line joblib save, load and predict-parity check.
traps: Calling fit_transform on the test set with the same pipeline object. It refits every statistic on evaluation data; call transform only.
Tuning the SelectFromModel threshold on the test score. The notebook run at 0.005 shows no gain; tune it under cross-validation or hold it fixed.
Saving the model but rebuilding preprocessing by hand in serving. Any median, category list or cluster center that differs silently shifts every prediction.

selfTest.q: Where does SelectFromModel sit relative to the cross-validation split, and what breaks if it sits outside?
selfTest.a: Inside, fit on training folds only. Outside, the selector sees evaluation labels and the error estimate turns optimistic.

selfTest.q: A new column appears in serving data. What does ColumnTransformer do with it?
selfTest.a: It drops it under remainder=drop. That is silent, so add a schema test that fails on unexpected columns.

selfTest.q: A joblib reload matches old predictions, but new-category rows differ from training time. Is the artifact broken?
selfTest.a: Not necessarily. handle_unknown=ignore maps new categories to all zeros by design. The parity check is identical predictions on fixed rows plus the declared unknown policy.
